Definition: to be (causatively, make) twinned, i.e. (figuratively) duplicate or (architectural) jointed
BiblicalUsage: The boards of the tabernacle were to be coupled together beneath, twinned and joined, so the frame stood as one. The Song uses the same picture for teeth, white and even, like a flock of sheep coming up from the washing, every one bearing twins. The word is doubling, joining: two made one, and made strong by it.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the tabernacle's twinned boards preach a quiet sermon: strength in God's house comes from being joined together, not from standing alone.
